input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV.I lets the Licensor unilaterally extend the Agreement for a further seven years, with no Licensee consent, no non-renewal notice window, and no cap on renewal fees. A multi-year renewal imposed at the Vendor's option falls in our walk-away zone and contradicts Article IV.II and III, which contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement. We therefore replaced it with successive twelve-month renewals by mutual written agreement and a CPI/3% cap on renewal fee increases; fallback would be automatic twelve-month renewals with a 60-day opt-out and a 5% cap.

proposal.summary: Replace unilateral 7-year Licensor-option renewal with 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement and a CPI/3% cap on renewal fees.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the seven-year renewal exercisable at Licensor's sole option with successive twelve-month renewals by mutual written agreement (consistent with Article IV.II and III) and capped any renewal fee increase at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Our position is that renewals must be mutual, no longer than twelve months, and predictably priced; if a longer commitment is needed we could accept twelve-month automatic renewals with a 60-day opt-out and increases capped at 5%.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive additional periods of twelve (12) months by mutual written agreement of the parties, and any increase in the fees payable for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding period and three percent (3%).
